title: NOVA3R: Non-pixel-aligned Visual Transformer for Amodal 3D Reconstruction
claim: Prior per-view aligned methods yield incomplete, duplicated geometry; our global non-aligned representation gives complete, physically plausible reconstructions.
layout: 2 rows, left-to-right flow, results in rounded boxes with red callouts
description: Two horizontal rows compare a pixel-aligned baseline (VGGT, top) with NOVA3R (bottom). In each row, two input photos of a desk scene feed a rounded module box. The top box, labeled Pixel-aligned, outputs two colored feature stacks (blue, orange) leading to a per-frame point cloud. The bottom box, Non-pixel-aligned, takes an initial scene token and outputs a single green stack leading to a global point cloud. Hollow arrows lead to two rounded panels on the right. The blue panel (Color by Depth) shows Visible Only versus Complete 3D. The purple panel (Color by Density) shows Duplicated versus Physically Plausible. Red boxes and arrows mark the incomplete region and the high-density duplicated region in the top row. Viridis and plasma colorbars run from 0 to 1. A dashed line separates the rows.
caption: \method enables non–pixel-aligned reconstruction by learning a global scene representation from unposed images. Compared to pixel-aligned methods, \method recovers both visible and occluded regions and produces more physically plausible geometry with fewer duplicated structures.
abstract: We present NOVA3R, an effective approach for non-pixel-aligned 3D reconstruction from a set of unposed images in a feed-forward manner. Unlike pixel-aligned methods that tie geometry to per-ray predictions, our formulation learns a global, view-agnostic scene representation that decouples reconstruction from pixel alignment. This addresses two key limitations in pixel-aligned 3D: (1) it recovers both visible and invisible points with a complete scene representation, and (2) it produces physically plausible geometry with fewer duplicated structures in overlapping regions. To achieve this, we introduce a scene-token mechanism that aggregates information across unposed images and a diffusion-based 3D decoder that reconstructs complete, non-pixel-aligned point clouds. Extensive experiments on both scene-level and object-level datasets demonstrate that NOVA3R outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of reconstruction accuracy and completeness.
